## 🧺 Laundry Process Redesign – Home Operations Case (OPMT 620)

<div class="project-card">

<div class="project-meta">
<strong>Course:</strong> OPMT 620 – Operations Management  
<strong>Type:</strong> Individual case study • Flow process chart • Lean waste analysis  
<strong>Tools:</strong> Flow process chart, waste analysis, process redesign
</div>

### Project Snapshot

I analysed my own home laundry routine as if it were a small “operations system.” I documented the **current-state process** using a flow process chart, tracking every operation, transport, delay, and inspection step, along with the **time**, **distance walked**, and **cost implications**. The original process took **138 minutes** and required **670 feet** of walking around the house. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}  

The key wastes I identified were:

- Excessive transportation (clothes moving between multiple rooms)  
- Waiting time during machine cycles  
- Over-processing and repeated handling (sorting and stain inspection done separately)  
- Inefficient layout and lack of standardization

### Improvements & Results

I then designed a **future-state process** that:

- Added laundry hampers in each room to reduce trips  
- Combined sorting and stain inspection into a single step  
- Used a wheeled laundry basket and detergent pods  
- Placed the washer and dryer side-by-side with a nearby folding station  

These changes cut total cycle time to **75 minutes** and reduced walking distance to **305 feet**, saving **63 minutes** and **365 feet** of movement per full laundry cycle, while making the work more ergonomic. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

</div>

## 🤖 UiPath & BMO – Banking Automation Case Study (CMPT 641)

<div class="project-card project-card-alt">

<div class="project-meta">
<strong>Course:</strong> CMPT 641 – Digital Transformation  
<strong>Type:</strong> Individual written assignment • Vendor analysis • Financial services case  
<strong>Tools:</strong> Secondary research, vendor comparison, value chain & benefits analysis
</div>

### Project Snapshot

For this assignment, I explored how **UiPath**, a leading robotic process automation (RPA) platform, helps the **Bank of Montreal (BMO)** modernise operations. I started with a vendor scan, comparing UiPath to competitors such as Microsoft Power Automate, Automation Anywhere, and Blue Prism, and summarised why UiPath holds a leading market share in RPA and strong analyst recognition. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}  

### Problem & Solution

BMO faced:

- Heavy manual workloads in compliance reporting, transaction monitoring, and testing  
- High operational costs and slower turnaround times  
- Fragmented legacy systems across different jurisdictions  

Working with UiPath and Deloitte, BMO built an **Automation Centre of Excellence (CoE)** and deployed unattended and attended bots for processes like loan origination, KYC/AML checks, and reporting. Bots were orchestrated via UiPath Studio and Orchestrator, integrated with Microsoft 365, Oracle, and internal banking systems. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}  

### Impact

The case highlighted how automation:

- Delivered **millions of dollars in value** through labour savings and cost avoidance  
- Achieved **20–60% productivity improvements** in some credit and back-office workflows  
- Reduced error rates and improved compliance audit trails  
- Freed employees to focus on more analytical and customer-facing work  

[📄 **View full report**](files/UiPath_BMO_Digital_Transformation_Case.pdf){target="_blank"}

</div>
